subject: Learning Methods
title: How Sleep Consolidates Memory
description: A quick win: understand How Sleep Consolidates Memory.

hook.text: Memories formed during the day are fragile and easily overwritten. Sleep transforms them into stable, long-lasting.

buildup.text: During waking hours, the hippocampus acts as a temporary notebook. It holds new memories until they can be properly.

discovery.text: During sleep, the hippocampus replays these memories and slowly transfers them to the neocortex for permanent storage.

twist.text: The transfer is selective. Emotionally important and repeatedly accessed memories get priority. Not everything is saved.

climax.text: Review important material before bed. This signals the brain that it matters, increasing the chance it'll.

punchline.text: Study before bed. Sleep moves it to permanent storage.

quiz.question: What determines which memories get consolidated during sleep?
options: Emotionally important and repeatedly accessed memories get priority
Only visual memories are consolidated during sleep
